answers.quote: The major and important rivers of the Northern Bengal are Mahananda, Teesta, Torsa, Jaldhaka, Kaljani, and Raidak. Generally, these rivers are perennial which means they have water throughout the year.
answers.notes: c13 lists Mahananda, Teesta, Torsa, Jaldhaka, Kaljani and Raidak as North Bengal's major perennial rivers.

answers.quote: The river has a length of 2,525 km. It is shared by Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh (1,450 km), Bihar (445 km) and West Bengal (520 km).
answers.notes: c03 gives West Bengal's share of the Ganga as 520 km.

answers.quote: It rises in the Gangotri glacier near Gaumukh (3,900 m) in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. Here, it is known as the Bhagirathi. At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda; hereafter, it is known as the Ganga.
answers.notes: c04: at Devprayag Bhagirathi meets Alaknanda and is then known as Ganga.

answers.quote: The Teesta River originates from the Chho Lhamo Lake in North Sikkim and flows through Sikkim and North Bengal before entering Bangladesh, eventually merging with the Brahmaputra.
answers.notes: c14: Teesta enters Bangladesh and merges with the Brahmaputra.

answers.quote: The Damodar occupies the eastern margins of the Chotanagpur Plateau where it flows through a rift valley and finally joins the Hugli. Once known as the 'sorrow of Bengal', the Damodar has been now tamed by the Damodar Valley corporation, a multipurpose project.
answers.notes: c07: Damodar finally joins the Hugli.

answers.quote: Barakar is a tributary of which River? Damodar.
answers.notes: c34: Barakar is a tributary of the Damodar.

answers.quote: A 2245 metre long Barrage across river Ganga, with 109 bays and a Head Regulator with 11 bays. A 213 metre long Barrage across river Bhagirathi at Jangipur with 15 bays. 38.38 km long Feeder Canal with carrying capacity of 1133 cumec (40,000 cusec).
answers.notes: c38 describes the Farakka barrage across the river Ganga.

answers.quote: The first dam was built across the Barakar River at Tilaiya and inaugurated in 1953. The second dam, Konar Dam, across the Konar River was inaugurated in 1955. The third dam across the Barakar River at Maithon was inaugurated in 1957. The fourth dam across the Damodar at Panchet was inaugurated in 1959. Durgapur Barrage was constructed downstream of the four dams in 1955, across the Damodar river at Durgapur.
answers.notes: c40: first DVC dam built at Tilaiya, inaugurated 1953.

answers.quote: The mouths of these mighty rivers also form some of the largest deltas of the world, for example, the famous Sunderbans delta.
answers.notes: c10: mouths of Ganga and Brahmaputra form the famous Sunderbans delta; c33 also places Sundarban Wetland in the delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra.

answers.quote: The Damodar occupies the eastern margins of the Chotanagpur Plateau where it flows through a rift valley and finally joins the Hugli. Once known as the 'sorrow of Bengal', the Damodar has been now tamed by the Damodar Valley corporation, a multipurpose project.
answers.notes: c07: Damodar once known as the 'sorrow of Bengal'.

answers.answer: শুধু বর্ষার বৃষ্টিতে চলে, তাই মরসুমি
answers.quote: In West Bengal, there are some rivers in the Western Plateau: Ajay, Mayurakshi, Damodar, Rupnarayan, Haldi, and Subarnarekha. Rivers originating from the plateau region, such as the Kansavati, depend on monsoon rains and often run dry during the dry months.
answers.notes: c24: western plateau rivers are rain-fed/seasonal; Kansavati-type plateau rivers depend on monsoon rain and run dry in dry months.

answers.quote: Murshidabad district is bisected into two halves by Bhagirathi river.
answers.notes: c21: Murshidabad district is bisected by the Bhagirathi.

answers.quote: The Mahananda is another important tributary of the Ganga rising in the Darjiling hills. It joins the Ganga as its last left bank tributary in West Bengal.
answers.notes: c06: Mahananda joins the Ganga as its last left bank tributary in West Bengal.

answers.quote: Bhagirathi-Hooghly river is known as the heart and soul of West Bengal. In West Bengal, the Hooghly river is the most important river from an economical and geographical point of view.
answers.notes: c22: Bhagirathi-Hooghly is the heart and soul of West Bengal (option is the Bengali rendering of that phrase).

answers.quote: Western part of Tista river is known as Terai. Punarbhava and Atrai are the distributaries of the Teesta.
answers.notes: c19: western part of Teesta is Terai (eastern part Duars).

answers.quote: Jalpaiguri town is located in the bank of Tista and Karala river.
answers.notes: c20: Jalpaiguri town is on the banks of Teesta and Karala.

answers.quote: The following river divides West Bengal and Assam: Sankosh.
answers.notes: c18: Sankosh divides West Bengal and Assam.

answers.quote: Torsa river originates from the Chumbi valley in Tibet and flows into Bhutan. It enters into India via Coochbehar district of West Bengal.
answers.notes: c15: Torsa originates in the Chumbi valley in Tibet.

answers.quote: The longest river of Western West Bengal is Damodar. Damodar river originates from the Khamarpath hill of the Chotanagpur plateau in Bihar. Damodar river flooded many areas of Bardhaman, Hooghly, Howrah, and East and West Midnapore districts thus it is alternatively known as the Sorrow of West Bengal.
answers.notes: c23: Damodar is the longest river of western West Bengal.

answers.quote: The Kasai and Keleghai rivers join to form the Haldi river.
answers.notes: c26: Kasai and Keleghai join to form the Haldi.

answers.quote: Kumari river is a tributary of Kansabati.
answers.notes: c27: Kumari is a tributary of the Kansabati.

answers.quote: Mukutmanipur Dam is located across the following river: Kangsabati. Mukutmanipur Dam is built at the confluence of Kangsabati and Kumari rivers.
answers.notes: c44: Mukutmanipur Dam is across the Kangsabati.

answers.quote: Teesta Barrage Project is one of the largest irrigation projects not only in West Bengal but also in the entire eastern region. It will create 9.22 lakh ha. of irrigation potential in six northern districts of West Bengal and 67.50 MW of hydropower from canal falls. The preliminary activities of 1st Sub-stage of Stage-I of Phase-I was started in the year 1975-76. Teesta Barrage at Gajoldoba, Block- Rajganj and Mal, District- Jalpaiguri. Pick up Barrage on River Mahananda at Fulbari in Rajganj Block in Jalpaiguri District. The drinking water supply for Siliguri Municipal Areas has been effected from the pond of the Mahananda Barrage.
answers.notes: c42: Teesta Barrage at Gajoldoba, Jalpaiguri district (Fulbari is the Mahananda pick-up barrage, a distractor).

answers.quote: A 2245 metre long Barrage across river Ganga, with 109 bays and a Head Regulator with 11 bays. A 213 metre long Barrage across river Bhagirathi at Jangipur with 15 bays. 38.38 km long Feeder Canal with carrying capacity of 1133 cumec (40,000 cusec).
answers.notes: c38: feeder canal is 38.38 km long.

answers.quote: The active delta of the Ganga in India lies here: North 24 Parganas and South 24 Parganas.
answers.notes: c30: active delta of the Ganga in India lies in North and South 24 Parganas.

answers.quote: Which one of the following rivers does not flow across the India-Bangladesh border? Damodar.
answers.notes: c35: Damodar does not cross the India-Bangladesh border; it joins the Hugli inside West Bengal.

answers.answer: দু'বার — গঙ্গোত্রীর ধারা ও ফারাক্কার পরের শাখা
answers.quote: It rises in the Gangotri glacier near Gaumukh (3,900 m) in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. Here, it is known as the Bhagirathi. At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda; hereafter, it is known as the Ganga.
answers.notes: Synthesis of claims: c04 uses Bhagirathi for the Gangotri-glacier stream that becomes Ganga at Devprayag, and c05 says the Ganga splits into the Bhagirathi and the Padma (the post-Farakka branch feeding the Bhagirathi-Hooghly system, cf. c36-c38). No single claim states the 'twice' count explicitly, hence LIKELY.

answers.quote: Western part of Tista river is known as Terai. Punarbhava and Atrai are the distributaries of the Teesta.
answers.notes: c19: Punarbhaba and Atrai are distributaries of the Teesta.

answers.quote: Jaldhaka River: Source: It originates in the Himalayas in south-east Sikkim, passes through Bhutan, passes through the Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri and Cooch Behar districts of West Bengal, India, enters Bangladesh and joins the Dharla River to join the Brahmaputra.
answers.notes: c16 gives Jaldhaka's full route: SE Sikkim Himalayas, Bhutan, Darjeeling/Jalpaiguri/Cooch Behar, then Bangladesh to the Brahmaputra.

answers.quote: Rupnarayan river originates from the foothills of the Chotanagpur plateau. It is also known as the Dwarakeswar river in Bankura. Kangsabati and Rupnarayan, formed by plateau streams uniting in Bankura and Paschim Medinipur, ultimately drain into the Hooghly estuary near Geonkhali.
answers.notes: not covered by claims: c25 only says Rupnarayan originates in Chotanagpur foothills and is called Dwarakeswar in Bankura; the Dwarakeswar+Shilabati confluence is not stated in any claim. Chosen by elimination (Kasai+Keleghai=Haldi per c26; Kangsabati+Kumari is the Mukutmanipur confluence per c44).

answers.quote: The drainage system of West Bengal is the recipient of three major rivers basins i.e., the Ganga, the Brahmaputra and the Subarnarekha covering 81%, 12% and 4% of the total area respectively.
answers.notes: c28: Subarnarekha basin covers 4% of West Bengal (Ganga 81%, Brahmaputra 12%).

answers.quote: The first dam was built across the Barakar River at Tilaiya and inaugurated in 1953. The second dam, Konar Dam, across the Konar River was inaugurated in 1955. The third dam across the Barakar River at Maithon was inaugurated in 1957. The fourth dam across the Damodar at Panchet was inaugurated in 1959. Durgapur Barrage was constructed downstream of the four dams in 1955, across the Damodar river at Durgapur.
answers.notes: c40 dates: Tilaiya 1953, Konar 1955, Maithon 1957, Panchet 1959.

answers.quote: The Massanjore dam (also called Canada Dam), across the Mayurakshi, was commissioned in 1955. Massanjore Dam is located on the Mayurakshi River near Dumka in Jharkhand. It was constructed with Canadian aid.
answers.notes: c43: Massanjore/Canada Dam across Mayurakshi near Dumka in Jharkhand.

answers.quote: Sundarban Wetland in West Bengal, designated on 30 January 2019, is India's largest Ramsar Site at 4,23,000 hectares. It encompasses hundreds of islands and a maze of rivers, rivulets and creeks in the delta of the rivers Ganges and Brahmaputra on the Bay of Bengal.
answers.notes: c33: Sundarban Wetland designated a Ramsar site on 30 January 2019.

answers.quote: Geomorphologists opine that change of the course of the Kosi river resulted in Kolkata Port declining.
answers.notes: c45: geomorphologists opine Kosi course change resulted in Kolkata Port declining.

answers.quote: The river has a length of 2,525 km. It is shared by Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh (1,450 km), Bihar (445 km) and West Bengal (520 km).
answers.notes: Statement 1 true (520 km in WB, c03); statement 2 false because Bihar's share is 445 km, less than West Bengal's 520 km (c03).

answers.quote: Damodar Valley Corporation was set up in 1948 as "the first multipurpose river valley project of independent India." It is modeled on the Tennessee Valley Authority of the United States. The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) is a government organization represented by both the central (India) and the state governments of West Bengal and Jharkhand.
answers.notes: c39: DVC came into being 7 July 1948 and was modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority of the USA.

answers.quote: Jaldhaka River: Source: It originates in the Himalayas in south-east Sikkim, passes through Bhutan, passes through the Darjeeling, Jalpaiguri and Cooch Behar districts of West Bengal, India, enters Bangladesh and joins the Dharla River to join the Brahmaputra.
answers.notes: Teesta-Sikkim Himalaya (c14), Torsa-Chumbi valley Tibet (c15), Jaldhaka-SE Sikkim Himalaya (c16, quoted), Raidak-Akungchu peak Bhutan (c17).

The third dam across the Barakar River at Maithon was inaugurated in 1957. The fourth dam across the Damodar at Panchet was inaugurated in 1959. Durgapur Barrage was constructed downstream of the four dams in 1955, across the Damodar river at Durgapur.
answers.notes: c40: Tilaiya 1953, Konar 1955, Maithon 1957, Panchet 1959.

answers.quote: Barakar is a tributary of which River? Damodar.
answers.notes: c34: Barakar is a tributary of the Damodar; other pairs contradict c27 (Kumari belongs to Kansabati) etc.

answers.answer: A ও R উভয়ই সত্য এবং R হল A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: The longest river of Western West Bengal is Damodar. Damodar river originates from the Khamarpath hill of the Chotanagpur plateau in Bihar. Damodar river flooded many areas of Bardhaman, Hooghly, Howrah, and East and West Midnapore districts thus it is alternatively known as the Sorrow of West Bengal.
answers.notes: c23 quote directly links Damodar's flooding of Bardhaman/Hooghly/Howrah/Midnapore to its 'Sorrow of West Bengal' name, so R explains A. The option containing 'সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা' without 'নয়' is the both-true-and-explains option.
